I switched on the automatic restart
if the bot closes or crashes, there's a job that'll run every 5 minutes (on every full 5) that will start it back up, unless it's explicitly set to not switch on
running ?restart restarts it automatically, running ?shutdown closes it and lets the scheduled job bring it back within 5 minutes

?shutdown [halt]

***Maintenance-only command***
Save all data and close the bot, and disable automatic restart.
Data persisted between bot runs:
- people's last locations
- most recent day on which each daily message was sent
- nicknames of active server members

By default, the bot will be automatically restarted within 5 minutes (on the next full 5 minutes mark).
To disable that behaviour, pass to the `halt` parameter value: `and halt, yes, seriously`
With halt state enabled, the automatic uptime script __**WILL NOT FIRE**__.
Halt state can only be switched off through manual access.
manual access = ssh to the server, or dropbox. it'll be a file `Dropbox/arcania/bot/savestates/_HALT_STATE`. remove it and the automatic restart will resume

Originally founded by the dutch, the first island to be settled was this, the dwarvish settlement of New Ampsterhold. As the other cities around New Ampsterhold began to thrive and look to one another for common governance,  Glaswegian Elves (Commonly called Weegies) came to an accord with the dwarvish mayoral council to found a single city made up of the 5 boroughs. Here at the heart of Empire, all of the other boroughs refer to the isle of Manhattan as simply "The City." They say the this solar punk metropolis has a true name inscribed by the dwarves and enchanted by the elves. But it's location remains a closely guarded secret.
The City is a Metropolis. It is wildly diverse, with its own city sized neighborhoods. It is crisscrossed by canals above the city, and a deep warren of jackalope built subways.

Verdant greenery grown by the Elves sits atop monumental towers of stone erected by masters of masonry and stone work. At night, it's lights glimmer on the inky black Hudson river. During the day, Airships above, steam powered paddle boats and sail boats below crisscross in an ever changing murmuration. Gliders and gondalas, submarines and skiffs, The City is defined by the motion of it's people.
The great boulevards, Wall and Broadway are the seats of wealth and entertainment for all of the colonies.

Deep below the city vast leylines converge, making it a veritable volcano of magical power. This fact makes The City the economic and engineering marvel that it is. It also makes for an ideal place to for the rebellion's minute men to make their last stand against the forces of King George's airship armada.

Hampstead, heart of Empire City.  Sure The City is clean and glorious, Ferrytown is chaotic beauty, Staaten is pure industry, and Kingsbridge is style and class.  But Hampstead, Hampstead is the rotten core of this city. Hampstead houses the first building in Empire City, the Empire City Gazette. The cornerstone of the Gazette, underneath layers of grease and grime are the words:
```Fear of loss drives all strife.
Truth is the only path to liberty.
Let Justice and Mercy be equal.```

That’s the entire borough though, grime, dust, dirt, with insects everywhere.  The buildings are made of wood and stone, with rarely a clean window to look out of.  The streets are uneven, cobbled with a mix of bricks and stone.  At night most of the lamps are lit, shedding dim yellow pools, just a bit too far apart. 

Hampstead’s weather is often hot, muggy, mildly overcast.  Just enough sun comes through the clouds to keep it hot, there is just enough clouds overhead to trap the heat and moisture in the air.  Thick fog rolls in at irregular times, making it difficult to breathe. People whisper about the fog being insidious.

The people of Hampstead walk with a hunch, like a weight is on the shoulders, like the air itself is heavy.  Joy seems to be universally absent from the faces of the people.  Illness is so commonplace in Hampstead that people have stopped even looking for cures.

Soldiers can be seen marching down every street,  filling every public space, listening in on every conversation.  They force themselves into homes and into beds.  They buy up all the goods, leaving overpriced, half rotten food for the people.  The stranglehold the British have on Hampstead is choking the very life from Empire City’s core.

But there are signs of rebellion.  In secret rooms, and private residences groups are found to be plotting against the occupation of their town.  The soldiers come down hard on the rebellion when they find them.  Graffiti pops up from time to time, its common to see soldiers forcing people to clean the following words off the walls:

```Like a plague of locusts they came. They came to our streets, our shops, our homes, they took from us, nearly starved us, and expected us to sit idly by silent in our suffering. But no more. Now we will become the locusts. We will take back what belongs to us, repulse them, overwhelm them. Consume them.```
As a deal with the warden Columbia, the Noir is a barrier between Empire City and the rest of the continent, making Kingsbridge the last line of defense for Arcania should Empire City fall.

Main NPC: Gaillardia, a Dryad 
Gaillardia is the mother of Herb, of Herb’s Herbs. They live together in this cozy little hut on a seaside cliff. Gaillardia is agoraphobic and never leaves her home and the surrounding gardens. She is no nonsense, a little grumbly, and is devoted to protecting her grove.
On the Edge of Illo’fae stands a cozy looking cottage nestled atop a seaside cliff. It is surrounded by all manner of trees, flowers, and other plants. Butterflies flit from bud to bud, catching the ocean breeze. 
Inside the cottage is cluttered with drying plants of all kinds, bubbling pots, and shelves and shelves of magical components. You see a cauldron bearing relief scenes of various heroes embossed on its sides. 
Gaillardia can bring one person back to life with this cauldron of rebirth every 7 days. This requires 200lbs (10g) of salt, various items of importance to the character being brought back, and one fae deal of the DMs choosing. 
Once adventurers are out gathering the necessary components Gaillardia will cast speak with dead on the PC being brought back. If a deal is not struck by the end of her questions, she will not bring them back. 
If a deal is struck, and ingredients successfully gathered, the spell will be complete 8 hours after the last ingredient is placed. Characters are encouraged to speak on behalf of their friend, reminding of who they are, what is left to accomplish, etc while the process is underway.

As the ferry departs from the harbor and the city fades behind you, a small old woman clambers up from the worker's area and grins to the passengers. She appears to be the old lady who collected your tickets, but that woman definitely had brown hair and you could have sworn she waved you off from the shore. You shrug it off. Probably just your eyes playing tricks on you, or maybe you misremembered.
"Now dearies, before we arrive at Ferrytown, there are some things ye best know." Her voice is old and creaky, and she has an accent both distinctive and unfamiliar. "I'm sure some of ye have heard the stories about strange creatures and mysterious happenings, but I can excitedly confirm that they are in fact, all true!" She pauses for a minute, observing the shock on your faces before breaking out into raucous laughter. 
"I'm joking, of course! Would hardly be able to have visitors if Ferrytown was everything the stories said we are." You notice that she seems to add in an extra y to the name this time. "Course, it ain't perfectly safe. No place is, these days. But ye stay in the main areas and don't wander into the wilder areas of our little district and ye should do just fine." The ferry begins to approach its destination, slowing down. 
"One last thing, dearies." She says with a grin. "In Ferrytown, if someone asks you 'can I have your name?', the polite response is 'no, but you can call me...'" Each person riding the ferry sees her wink at specifically them, before she ducks back to the underbelly from whence she came.

When you finally step off into the town, you can see her already on shore, boarding passengers for the return trip. Her hair is blonde, rather than grey or brown, and she appears to be in the midst of a conversation that has been going on for quite some time. You shake off the strange feeling and wander off into the metropolis.
Ferrytown, also known as Feytown or Feyrytown to the locals, is the most natural burrough due to its series of 'bleeds', areas where the feywild bleeds over into the material plane, creating pockets of vibrant colors, intoxicating smells, beautiful flora and fauna, and denizens not typically found on this plane. These areas are mostly home to the more fantastical residents of Ferrytown, though peoples of all types live across the burrough. Many of these areas are seen as parks, and fulfill that function for many of the residents as well as visitors. The most notorious use of these bleeds, however, is their application in smuggling. The grassy bay bleed being a patchwork of the material plane and the feywild means that it is difficult to track and follow shipments in and out, especially when the smugglers are much more connected to the area than those pursuing them.

There are no bridges to or from ferrytown, as all transport not by land is done by ferry. As the burrough is largely known for its transport by water, both of people and goods, the burrough has three separate ports, not counting the grassy bay bleed. All sorts of goods pass in, out, and through Ferrytown, though there is one exception: iron. Creatures from the feywild, particularly fey, find iron unpleasant to the point of it hurting when they make contact with it. As such, ferrytown does not trade in iron, and its use is frowned upon in the burrough. The buildings, tools, weapons, and armor in ferrytown are not constructed from iron or iron-based metals, and are instead largely built from wood and glass. The wood comes from various trees throughout, though the largest and best-known tree is Cael’fii, or the gentle mother.
The tesslotyl powered steam engines run at regular intervals through out the city.
A hub for the poor and creative, the outcasts and those starving for their art, Greenwitch village is where hope and suffering in equal measures mix.

The woman gives you a small smile and a pat on the back and says: “Apologies, little comrade, may your muscles do better in future.”
**DC15**- A tank top with a super strong torso on it (mens or womens)
DC 19- Nolzur’s magical warpaint 1 dose (paint this on your face and become immune to fear for 1 hour)
The woman raises her eyebrow as she takes out your prize. “Not bad, you vould do in  fight against nieces maybe.” She hands you a small vile marked ‘Nolzur’s warpaint- single use’.
**DC 23**- Gloves of the Goliath (push/drag/lift one size larger)
The woman smiles a big smile and before you know what is happening she is slapping you on the back with a force you did not expect. “Impressive vork! You almost strong like me, these help.” She hands you a pair of grey gloves with various black markings.

You walk up and you see a booth that at first seems to be well stocked with furry prizes, but upon closer inspection the furry prizes are moving and appear to be… manning the booth? They scurry to and fro and when they see you, you hear a squeal of enjoyment, their little hands beckoning you closer. They motion to three bottles on a table at the back of the booth, and place three rings on the counter before you.
